ordered_diagnoses: Eosinophilia with Abnormal Vitamin B12 Metabolism

facts.raw_span: asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules
symmetrically distributed
lesions did not coalesce
face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected
hypereosinophilia (4220/μL; reference range 50-250/μL)
elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL; reference range <11.5 ng/mL)
elevated vitamin B12 (>6000 pg/mL; reference range 211-911 pg/mL)
no pathologic findings on CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis
no pathologic findings on cranial MRI
nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in upper dermis
FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene positive on RT-PCR
hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia

concepts.why: The patient's hypereosinophilia, FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene positivity, and hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia are consistent with Chronic Eosinophilic Leukemia.
The patient's elevated tryptase and nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in the skin are consistent with Mastocytosis.
The patient's nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in the skin is consistent with Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis.
The patient's hypereosinophilia and hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia are consistent with a Myeloproliferative Neoplasm.
The patient's nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in the skin and hypereosinophilia are consistent with Histiocytosis with Eosinophilia.
The patient's hypereosinophilia and nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in the skin are consistent with Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis.
The patient's hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia is consistent with Polycythemia Vera.
The patient's hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia is consistent with Primary Myelofibrosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Eosinophilia with Abnormal Vitamin B12 Metabolism
concepts.why: Elevated vitamin B12 levels are a characteristic finding in certain myeloproliferative disorders, particularly those with eosinophilia, which is consistent with the patient's laboratory results.

rationales.F01: Asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules are common in histiocytosis and eosinophilic disorders
rationales.F05: Hypereosinophilia is a key feature of chronic eosinophilic leukemia and other eosinophilic disorders
rationales.F06: Elevated tryptase is often seen in mastocytosis and other mast cell disorders
rationales.F07: Elevated vitamin B12 is associated with eosinophilia and abnormal vitamin B12 metabolism
rationales.F11: FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene is diagnostic of chronic eosinophilic leukemia
